messages:
maria: heads-up — ricochet13b (int8) canary started showing OOM spikes on P100 pool and a small eval-quality regression on our summarization suite. logs attached below.
chris: saw the OOMs too. looks like fragmentation after ~3500 tokens of conversation. batch size was 6, max_new_tokens 256.
jordan: do we have the exact memstats? rough numbers?
maria: paste from a canary host: ```OOM: cudaMemcpy failed, free: 48MB, allocated: 95GB, total GPU: 96GB
KV cache highwater: 78GB
Slots free before request: 3
Request tokens: 4200 (history included)
Batch size: 6, max_new_tokens: 256```
kai: that KV highwater is worrying. ricochet has longer past context defaults. Did quantization change per-layer memory layout?
maria: int8 pack changed kernel alignment — combined with our slab allocator it increases fragmentation on sequences > 2k. We hit many small free segments.
chris: can we mitigate by lowering default max_new_tokens to 128 for ricochet13b in hosted catalog? should help typical chats and reduce KV growth.
jordan: agree. also suggest soft cap per-session: if history len + max_new_tokens > 3000, reject or ask to truncate. Quick patch: ```if (context_estimate > 3000) return TRUNCATE_RESPONSE```
kai: also try microbatching tweak: batch_size 6 -> dynamic microbatch where we split large-history requests into single-item microbatches for token generation stage. That avoids large simultaneous KV peaks.
maria: ran a quick experiment: dynamic microbatch + max_new_tokens 128 reduced mem highwater from 78GB -> 60GB and no OOMs across 1000 synthetic long-chat requests. perf penalty ~6% p50 latency.
chris: quality regression on summarization — is it from int8 quant or the max_new_tokens change? The eval showed BLEU/ROUGE drop of ~1.3 points.
maria: isolated: when running int8 quant with max_new_tokens 256 the model produced the same drop even with batch_size 1, so quant likely to blame.
jordan: fallback plan: for strips flagged by high-quality evals, route to int4-hybrid or full-fp16 variant. we can add routing policy: prefer int8, but on regressions serve fp16 for queries tagged "summary".
kai: propose rollout plan: - change hosted default max_new_tokens to 128 for ricochet13b (canary) - enable dynamic microbatch in runtime config (canary) - mark summarization route as quality-protected -> fallback to fp16 if eval drift detected - run 48h soak with 10k varied prompts
maria: I'll open the PR for default and microbatch toggle. also adding a quick eval set that focuses on long-context summaries and QA.
chris: add a metric alert: OOM count > 0.1% over 10m and eval ROUGE drop > 0.5 triggers rollback. deploy-bot: canary deployment queued.
deploy-bot: canary started 2026-03-23T15:24Z; groups: eng-staging; config: ricochet13b:int8 max_new_tokens=128 microbatch=dynamic routing=canary
maria: thanks — collecting more logs. if soak looks good, we'll prod rollout next week. :thumbsup:
